newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Miners BHP, RTZ-CRA closely watch PNG crisis.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Miners BHP, RTZ-CRA closely watch PNG crisis.

text.p: Two of crisis-hit Papua New Guinea's biggest investors, mining giants RTZ-CRA and The Broken Hill Pty Co, said on Monday they were closely following events in the country.
But spokesmen for RTZ-CRA, which has interests in the defunct Bougainville copper mine and new Lihir gold project, and BHP, which controls the Ok Tedi copper mine, declined to make any other comment.
Earlier, PNG army chief Jerry Singirok called for the resignation of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan within 48 hours because of his plans to use foreign mercenaries on Bougainville.
"We are just gathering the facts to understand what's happening," BHP spokesman Vincent Bull told Reuters by telephone from the Papua New Guinea capital, Port Moresby.
"We are watching the PNG situation," CRA spokesman Ian Head said. He declined to make any further comment.
Singirok has said his called for Chan's resignation does not amount to an army coup. He called on the country's governor-general to appoint a caretaker government.
